extracted.intended_audience: agencies, brands, marketers and producers submitting case films/campaign entries to the Cannes Lions Creative Effectiveness awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and judging criteria for submitting work to the Cannes Lions Creative Effectiveness awards, including eligibility, category definitions, required evidence of business impact, and judging weightings. It guides entrants on which category/market/sector to enter and what evidence and storytelling to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall purpose of entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The Creative Effectiveness Lions celebrate the measurable impact of creative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how an effective strategy rooted in creativity has met its chosen business objectives, generated positive customer outcomes and driven sustainable business impact over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of criteria will be considered during judging, weighted as follows: 25% idea; 25% strategy; 50% impact and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries will be assessed on idea, strategy and—most heavily—impact and results; entrants should prioritise clear, measurable evidence of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: previous Cannes Lions recognition required
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible your work must have won or been shortlisted at Cannes Lions in 2023, 2024 or 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only work with prior Cannes Lions shortlist/win in the specified years can be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry frequency and duplication limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work can be entered up to four times in Creative Effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the same piece of work may only be entered once in ‘A. Creative Effectiveness: Sectors’. In section A specifically: 'The same entry can be submitted only once in this section.' Entrants should plan category submissions to respect these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtitles recommendation for films and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtitles are highly recommended on all case films, films, demo films and original content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subtitles to improve accessibility and comprehension of audiovisual case materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section A: Focus on sector effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in this section should focus on effectiveness achieved in a particular sector, and whether the work achieved or exceeded its objectives and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must demonstrate sector-specific effectiveness and show how objectives/goals were met or exceeded; each entry may be submitted only once in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: A01 Consumer Goods: scope and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: All fast-moving and durable consumer goods, including but not limited to food and beverages, toiletries, cleaning products, other household goods, other FMCGs, clothing and accessories, furniture, and consumer electronics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: All fast-food entries should be entered into A04. Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: A02 Healthcare: scope and charity routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharma, OTC drugs, wellness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work has been created for a Charity/NFP then this should be entered into A07.

rubrics_metrics.name: A03 Automotive: scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Vehicles, other automobiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: A04 Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains: scope
rubrics_metrics.description: All transport- and travel-related services, including public transport and tourism boards. All entertainment- and leisure-related services, including museums, festivals and gyms. All shops, including online shopping, opticians, hairdressers and estate agents. All restaurants and fast food chains, including cafés and bars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fast-food entries (redirect from A01). Ensure category choice matches the product/service type.

rubrics_metrics.name: A05 Media/Entertainment: scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Music, film, television, publications and media, books, news, digital platforms and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: A06 Consumer Services/Business to Business: scope
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercial public services, legal, financial, B2B technology, consultancies and professional services, other business services, internal and corporate communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: A07 Not-for-Profit / Charity / Government: scope and CSR guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Government, public information, NGOs, military, charities, non-profit organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work is corporate social responsibility, enter in the relevant sector and/or B04. Creative Effectiveness for Good category in section B. Market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B: Market — demonstrate market-specific effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in this section should demonstrate how it enabled the brand to effectively achieve their objectives in a chosen market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the creative work was designed for the market(s) and provide tangible business results tied to that market strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: B01 Single Market: requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that has been implemented in a single market with a single target market at its core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should describe how it was designed for the target market and how the tangible business results were achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: B02 Multi-Market: requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that has been implemented across multiple markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should describe how it was designed for multiple markets and how the tangible business results were achieved (cross-market design and results evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: B03 Global Market: requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that has been implemented globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should describe how it was creatively designed to run globally and how the tangible business results were achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: B04 Creative Effectiveness for Good: social purpose requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating the measurable impact of creative work with social purpose at the heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should be for a charity, non-profit or government body or for brands who can demonstrate they worked in partnership with a not-for-profit organisation. The work should illustrate how the campaign drove tangible results and was instrumental to cultural change or integral to achieving a brand's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section C: Brand Challenges & Opportunities — focus on strategic response
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in these categories should focus on the brand challenge or opportunity identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should explain its strategic response, as well as specific channels and touchpoints chosen and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: C01 Launch: launch-focused work
rubrics_metrics.description: Work created to launch a product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the launch strategy and creative drove awareness, consideration and measurable objectives related to the launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: C02 Rebrand: rebrand/refresh work
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebrand/refresh of an existing brand identity for any product, service or organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate strategic rationale, creative execution and measurable outcomes of the rebrand.

rubrics_metrics.name: C03 Acquisition: new-customer acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that effectively attracts new customers or drives new engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should show an increase in new business or customer activity; provide clear metrics evidencing acquisition impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: C04 Retention: customer retention work
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that enhances or strengthens existing customer relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should show an increase in new business or customer activity (metrics demonstrating retention/engagement outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: C05 Real-Time Response: reactive work
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective targeted work that responds to world events, public affairs and other real-world, real-time activity prompting social sharing and a measurable response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate timeliness, relevance, social sharing metrics and measurable response tied to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: C06 Sustained Success: long-running campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating the long-term impact of creative work. The work should demonstrate how a long running campaign drove tangible business results, was instrumental to cultural change or integral to achieving a brand’s purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work in this category must show results over several years; provide longitudinal evidence of sustained impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: C07 Collaboration: collaborative work effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating the measurable impact of creative work that is the result of a collaboration between brands and agencies or partner agencies to achieve a business goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how the collaborative effort drove tangible business results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section D: Culture & Context — cultural/regional insight requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that is brought to life through cultural insights and regional context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should show how cultural or regional insight informed strategy and creative execution to drive effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: D01 Breakthrough on a Budget: low-budget creative impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative use of modest budgets and/or resources in relation to the market and/or industry to create maximum impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should demonstrate how fresh insight, smart spending and compelling strategic thinking solved a business problem despite limited resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: D02 Challenger Brand: competitive-response creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their approach in response to competitor pressure by challenging the status quo to create game-changing work that uses progressive thinking and innovative creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the approach challenged norms and drove measurable brand/business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: D03 Market Disruption: strategy adapted to issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their strategy in response to local / regional / global issues, embracing new ways of delivering their brand while showing consideration for the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate strategic adaptation, new delivery methods and consumer consideration, with evidence of business impact.
